target: Πάει στο σχολείο με τα πόδια.
english: He goes to school on foot.
tip: English says 'on foot'; Greek says with the feet – με τα πόδια (me ta podia), article included.

english: In the afternoon I go to the bakery.
tip: σε (se) + τον (ton) fuse into στον (ston) with masculine nouns: πάω στον φούρνο (páo ston foúrno = I go to the bakery).

target: Έρχομαι στο σπίτι σου το βράδυ.
english: I am coming to your house in the evening.
tip: Some verbs only exist in the -ομαι (-ome) form: έρχομαι (érchome = I come). The unusual ending changes nothing – the meaning is a plain action.

english: We are coming from Athens.
tip: Cities take 'the': από την Αθήνα (apo tin Athina) is literally 'from the Athens'. Countries too – η Ελλάδα (i Ellada).

english: I wake up at seven every day.
tip: Clock times are 'at the...': στις εφτά (stis efta) = at seven. The 'the' is plural because hours count as plural in Greek.

english: I am working from home today.
tip: One present tense does both English ones: δουλεύω (doulevo) = 'I work' and 'I am working'. Greek has no separate -ing form.

target: Μιλάω με τη μητέρα μου κάθε βράδυ.
english: I speak with my mother every evening.
tip: Possession keeps the article and puts 'my' after: τη μητέρα μου (ti mitera mou) = 'the mother of-me'. Μου (mou) never comes before the noun.

english: In the evening we watch television.
tip: Time of day needs no 'in': το βράδυ (to vradi) = in the evening, literally just 'the evening'. Mornings match: το πρωί (to proi).

english: I will go to the bank tomorrow.
tip: The future is just θα (tha) + verb: θα πάω (tha pao) = I will go. Θα never changes – one little word for every person and verb.

english: I will not be working on Thursday.
tip: Negative future has a fixed order – δεν (den) before θα (tha): Δεν θα δουλεύω (den tha doulévo = I will not be working).

english: I like Greek coffee.
tip: Liking flips the roles: the thing pleases you. Μου αρέσει ο καφές (mou arési o kafés = the coffee pleases me = I like coffee).

english: I like cheese a lot.
tip: Liking flips in Greek: μου αρέσει πολύ το τυρί (mou aresi poli to tiri) = 'the cheese pleases me a lot'. You're the receiver, not the doer.

target: Της αρέσει να μαγειρεύει για όλους.
english: She likes to cook for everyone.
tip: Liking to DO something adds να (na) + verb: Της αρέσει να μαγειρεύει (tis arési na magirévi = cooking pleases her = she likes to cook).

target: Μου αρέσει να διαβάζω το βράδυ.
english: I like to read in the evening.
tip: Greek has no infinitive – after να (na) the verb still conjugates: μου αρέσει να διαβάζω (mou aresi na diavazo) = 'I like that I read'.

english: I paid the bill by card.
tip: No word for 'by' with cards, just με: πλήρωσα με κάρτα (plírosa me kárta = I paid by card).

target: Δοκίμασα το παντελόνι, αλλά ήταν μικρό.
english: I tried on the trousers, but they were small.
tip: The event is a one-off, so δοκίμασα (dokímasa = I tried on); the description keeps the ongoing past: ήταν μικρό (ítan mikró = it was small).

target: Η Ελένη ψώνισε μόνη της χθες το απόγευμα.
english: Eleni shopped by herself yesterday afternoon.
tip: 'By herself' agrees with the person: μόνη της (móni tis) for a woman, μόνος του (mónos tou) for a man.

english: Did you eat anything at lunchtime?
tip: In questions τίποτα means 'anything': Έφαγες τίποτα; (éfages típota = did you eat anything?)

target: Δοκίμασα τη χωριάτικη και μου άρεσε πολύ.
english: I tried the Greek salad and liked it a lot.
tip: Liking in the past: μου άρεσε (mou árese = I liked it), literally 'it pleased me'.

english: I booked a table for nine o'clock.
tip: κλείνω (klíno) means both 'close' and 'book': έκλεισα τραπέζι (éklisa trapézi = I booked a table).

target: Δεν έφαγα τίποτα σήμερα το πρωί.
english: I didn't eat anything this morning.
tip: Greek stacks negatives: δεν έφαγα τίποτα (den éfaga típota = I didn't eat anything) is literally 'not I-ate nothing' – both words are required.

target: Ζήτησα τον λογαριασμό από τον σερβιτόρο.
english: I asked the waiter for the bill.
tip: You ask a thing FROM a person in Greek: ζήτησα από τον σερβιτόρο (zítisa apó ton servitóro = I asked from the waiter).

english: Last year we went on holiday to Crete.
tip: No 'on' with holidays: πήγαμε διακοπές (pígame diakopés = we went on holiday) – διακοπές attaches straight to the verb.

target: Το αεροπλάνο έφυγε στην ώρα του.
english: The plane left on time.
tip: στην ώρα του = on time, literally 'at its hour': έφυγε στην ώρα του (éfyge stin óra tou).

target: Έκλεισα τα εισιτήρια για το καλοκαίρι.
english: I booked the tickets for the summer.
tip: Booking is closing in Greek: έκλεισα τα εισιτήρια (ékleisa ta eisitíria = I booked the tickets). κλείνω (kleíno) also books tables and hotel rooms.

target: Χάσαμε το τρένο για την Αθήνα!
english: We missed the train to Athens!
tip: χάνω (cháno) covers both 'lose' and 'miss': χάσαμε το τρένο (chásame to tréno = we missed the train).

english: The trip took three hours.
tip: κρατάω also means 'to last': κράτησε τρεις ώρες (krátise treis óres = it lasted three hours).

target: Μείναμε σε ένα μικρό ξενοδοχείο κοντά στην παραλία.
english: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach.
tip: μένω is both live and stay: μείναμε σε ξενοδοχείο (meíname = we stayed).

english: I got back home the night before last.
tip: After motion verbs, home needs no 'to' or article: γύρισα σπίτι (gírisa spíti = I returned home) – just the bare word.

english: We had a wonderful time in the village.
tip: A good time 'passes' in Greek: Περάσαμε υπέροχα (perásame ypérocha = we passed wonderfully = we had a wonderful time).
